title: Time Zone and UTC Converter
description: The server stores times in UTC and converts school-local times with the offset in force on that date: in Chicago, CDT (UTC-5) from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November, and CST (UTC-6) otherwise. On the two change days some local times are awkward: 2:30 AM on the spring day does not exist, and 1:30 AM on the fall day happens twice. Two fixed rules decide them.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy
Configuring the School Agent and Calendar

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the UTC time of 8 school-local times, including 3 that fall at a daylight-saving change, with at least 7 of the 8 exactly right.
prerequisites: UTC, time zone, daylight saving time, offset, CDT, CST, EDT, a time that does not exist, a time that happens twice (all defined in the section "Time Zones and Daylight Saving" above this block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Is the offset from UTC the same all year?
What happens to a local time that does not exist?
Why are 8:00 in Chicago and 9:00 in New York the same instant on October 20?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The offset from UTC is the same all year. (2) A time that does not exist is an error. (3) A time that happens twice has no answer. (4) The same wall-clock time in two cities is the same instant.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all eight items. Mastery is 7 of 8 exactly right on the first attempt.
